title: Patchwork condenser feedback spike and request ledger
content:
Executive summary:

This is a compact recording of a 5-day feedback spike (Apr 26–May 2) where CS, Solutions Eng, and a few SREs pulled together emergent customer asks across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. Goal: produce a short list of high-leverage fixes we can action in the next 4–8 weeks and a separate longer backlog of architectural asks.

Methodology / dataset: rough pull from support tickets (n≈230), 3 customer calls (Enterprise, Mid-market, and AI-native), 2 internal triage sessions, and quick telemetry sampling (latency p50/p95 per model route). Notes are intentionally rough — think working notebook not polished artifact.

Key takeaways (top line):
- Repeated pain: unpredictable tail latency for bursty conversational workloads when KV-cache warms cold (affects Hosted + Dedicated).
- Cost friction: customers building high-throughput embedding pipelines want clearer per-embedding unit cost guidance and an easy warm-cache path (batching/caching presets).
- Observability gap: token-level cost breakdowns exist but customers want route-level SLA mapping and easy correlation to traces/spans (surface errors -> model fallback).
- Rollouts: canary A/B semantics are not expressive enough for multi-model fallbacks; customers fear silent quality regressions during model rollouts.
- Private deployment asks cluster around simpler KMS onboarding and clearer audit log sampling controls.

Sections below: grouped asks, representative customer quotes, quick fixes (4–8 weeks), medium-term proposals (2–3 quarters), owners + suggested priority, open questions and next steps.

1) Latency & KV-cache warming
- Frequency: high (≈40% of tickets sampled)
- Representative quotes:
  • “We see great median latency but the 95th spikes when our chat sessions start — seems cache miss related.” — fintech enterprise
  • “If a user opens a new conversation the initial response is 4–5x slower than the rest; it kills the UX.” — AI-native startup
- Quick fixes:
  • Add a configurable pre-warm endpoint for high-cardinality prefixes (team: eng-serving-runtime). Simple contract: POST prefixes -> warm for next 30m. Low-risk feature and aligns with existing cache APIs.
  • Add telemetry flag to tag requests that triggered cold-KV-warm. Emit metric and log with request id. (owner: obs-team; dependency: minor runtime change).
- Longer-term proposals:
  • Workload-aware prefetching: runtime learns hot prefixes and pre-warms on idle GPU time. Needs infra cost model.
  • Per-customer warm pools for Dedicated tenants (financially commitable option).
- Risk/Notes: warm endpoint increases memory usage; need quota and TTL policies.

2) Cost transparency for embeddings and batch pricing
- Frequency: medium-high (≈25%)
- Quotes:
  • “Our embedding pipeline is cheap to run but we can’t explain monthly spikes to finance.” — mid-market analytics team
  • “Bulk ingestion should have a defined warm/cold pricing policy; today it’s a black box.” — marketplace app
- Quick fixes:
  • Publish a sample cost-per-embedding spreadsheet for common batch sizes and model families (product + finance).
  • Add a ‘batch_hint’ param to the API that triggers recommended batching and returns estimated unit price for the request. Low effort: SDK change + price calc.
- Longer-term:
  • Introduce tiered batch discounts + explicit contract for Dedicated customers (requires pricing review).

3) Observability: route-level SLAs and trace linking
- Frequency: medium (≈18%)
- Quotes:
  • “We get token billing and top-level latency but it’s hard to find which route/config caused a regression.” — platform team at enterprise
- Quick fixes:
  • Console: add per-route SLA view that maps p50/p95 to time ranges and links to the last 5 errors (owner: product-console).
  • Add auto-linking between trace ids (from runtime) and console request views; enable one-click jump to span.
- Longer-term:
  • Alerting rules template: pre-built SLO->PagerDuty mapping for common regressions.

4) Rollouts, model fallback semantics, and quality guardrails
- Frequency: medium-high (≈30%)
- Quotes:
  • “When you roll a new model it’s hard to specify a shadow fallback sequence — we want explicit policy: if new model fails or falls below eval, go to fallback chain.” — security enterprise
- Quick fixes:
  • Add a ‘fallback_chain’ field to rollout configs allowing 1–2 backups and a health-check window for automatic fallback. Minimal UI + API extension.
  • Expose evaluation hooks that run a small prompt set (customer provided) during canary and report pass/fail percentage.
- Longer-term:
  • Canary orchestration: allow gradual traffic ramp with quality-based gating (not just percent-based). Requires eval infra and stronger telemetry.

5) Private deployments: KMS onboarding and audit sampling
- Frequency: high among private prospects (≈22% of private conversations)
- Quotes:
  • “KMS integration took us two weeks — we expected a single-day plug.” — regulated customer
  • “Audit logs are huge; we don’t need every token trace retained forever.” — on-prem operator
- Quick fixes:
  • Produce a step-by-step KMS runbook (docs + recipes for common providers) and a short onboarding checklist for SEs.
  • Add audit-sampling config in Private UI: sample rate by event type (owner: private-deployments + docs).
- Longer-term:
  • Native HSM connector path for top-tier enterprise and auto-validated compliance test harness.

6) Developer experience / prompt ergonomics and SDKs
- Frequency: moderate (≈15%)
- Notes:
  • Customers ask for more examples showing streaming + function-calls + structured output in multi-step flows.
- Quick fixes:
  • Add three canonical recipes to the SDK: streaming chat with KV-warm, embedding large-batch best-practices, and rollout guard example. Small doc + code change.

Action items and owners (first 4–8 week window):
- Warm endpoint MVP: eng-serving-runtime -> owner: Aiden Cho; milestone: design doc by 2027-05-10; implementation spike 2 weeks. Priority: P0 for bursty chat customers.
- Telemetry tag for cold-warm: obs-team -> owner: Priya Nandakumar; milestone: sample telemetry end-to-end 2027-05-20. Priority: P1.
- Cost-per-embedding guide + batch_hint: product-hosted-api + finance -> owner: Lena Hoffman; deliverable: public guide + SDK param in 3 weeks. Priority: P1.
- Per-route SLA console widget: product-console -> owner: Carlos Mendes (noted in linked artifacts); check feasibility 2027-05-12. Priority: P2.
- Private KMS runbook: solutions-eng -> owner: Marisol Vega; deliverable: runbook v1 2027-05-14. Priority: P1.

Open questions / unknowns:
- How much cache warming can we do without blowing up memory on shared pools? (need cost model from infra).
- For batch_hint pricing: does finance prefer a deterministic formula or model-family lookup table?
- Can we automate the canary eval hook without adding too much cold-call latency?

Notes to self / follow-ups:
- Validate warm endpoint contract with 2 large customers (FinTech and Marketplace) — CS to schedule.
- File a pre-req RFC for quota/TTL on warm entries (infra + runtime).
- Loop in pricing for Dedicated warm pools — sales input needed.
- Pull sample traces for three customers showing cold-warm delta and attach to JIRA-CCS-5712.

Appendix: raw excerpts (unedited)
- “We shy away from continuous conversations because the first message is always slow and users think the app froze.”
- “If we could pre-warm based on user id fingerprinting that would be huge.”
- “Embedding spikes align with our weekly batch job — having batch pricing and a warm window would reduce surprises.”

End of spike notes — these are intentionally compact and operational. Next doc should be a short proposal for the warm-endpoint design + telemetry proof-of-concept.

--Marisol
